decision.actionLabel: Hand NBL-016 to Dorian Pike: no working smoke alarm for 46 days, a possibly vulnerable occupant who asked for no contact, and an unknown visitor. Chase the landlord and send the tenant one reply about the visitor in the same turn.
decision.recipient: Dorian Pike (Maintenance Operations Lead, Northbridge Lettings)
decision.message:
Dorian, NBL-016 (26 Tallowmere Close) needs a decision from you. Summary below.

1. Smoke alarm. The tenant reported on 7 Aug that it had come away from the ceiling (E001). The landlord, Ronan Vale, chose to use his own electrician (E004). On 12 Aug he said the work would be done "by the following weekend at the latest" (E007). That did not happen. A fitter came on about 2 Sept, removed the bracket and could not refit the alarm because the box had no bracket in it. No return visit was booked (E010). We have no evidence that the alarm is mounted or tested (E014). The landlord has not written since 12 Aug, and we have no chase to him on file after E005.

2. Occupant. The tenant was admitted to hospital (E012) and discharged on 11 Sept. She asked us to stop the repeated calls and emails while she recovers (E013). We paused contact (E014). Her health details must not be passed to the landlord or anyone else.

3. Unknown visitor. On Saturday 20 Sept the tenant rang to report an unannounced person at the door who said they were there to "check something". She did not let them in because she could not verify who they were (E015). She says she had raised this before with another agency contact, who passed it to a building-management contact. Neither contact is named, and nobody has verified the visitor's identity or authority (E016).

What I have done in this turn:
- Chased the landlord by email (no health details). I asked who the electrician is, whether a bracket has been ordered, the date to refit and test the alarm, and whether he sent anyone on 20 Sept. Reply requested by Wed 24 Sept.
- Sent the tenant one short email, no reply needed. It thanks her for reporting the visitor, says she was right not to let them in, and tells her we will update her by Wed 24 Sept.

Decisions I need from you:
(a) Given how long the alarm has been off and the occupant's circumstances, do we step in? For example, ask the landlord to approve our contractor to fit and test an alarm now, or take it up with him by phone and at a more senior level.
(b) How do we handle the visitor report? Do we follow up with the unnamed building-management contact, and does this need security or police advice?
(c) How should we contact the tenant from now on, given her request for no contact?

I recommend (a): phone the landlord today. If he cannot give a firm date for the refit within 48 hours, ask him to approve our contractor to make the alarm safe.
decision.rationale: The case falls under escalation triggers in both manuals. A smoke alarm has been missing for about 46 days with no evidence of refitting or testing (E010, E014). The occupant may be vulnerable after a hospital stay (E012, E013) and has asked for no contact. An unverified person tried to get in (E015, E016). Choosing whether to step in on a job the landlord is managing, whether to break the tenant's contact pause, and how to deal with a possible security threat all need human judgement. In line with refinement 6, I am still sending the routine items myself: the landlord chase is overdue by weeks (E005, E007), and the tenant is owed a reply about the visitor she reported (E015). That reply is a single message that asks nothing of her.
decision.expectedOutcome: Dorian Pike decides whether to step in on the alarm and how to handle the visitor and contact with the tenant. The landlord replies with the electrician's details and a date to refit the alarm, and says whether he sent anyone on 20 Sept. The tenant knows we are checking and will hear from us by 24 Sept.
boundaries: Escalating does not make the alarm safe. There is still no evidence it is mounted or tested.
This does not settle who the visitor was or whether they were linked to the alarm work.
No contractor is approved or instructed. The landlord still manages the repair until he or Dorian Pike decides otherwise.
The tenant's health details are not shared with the landlord or any third party.
No date for the repair is promised to the tenant.

Dorian Pike to decide on stepping in, how to handle the visitor, and how to contact the tenant.
Update the tenant by 24 Sept with whatever has been confirmed.
Get evidence that the alarm has been refitted and tested before closing.

Because the tenant rang us on 20 Sept to report the visitor, one reply with no demands on her is acceptable despite her contact pause.
The landlord's email address used in E003–E007 is still current.

final.message:
Dorian, NBL-016 (26 Tallowmere Close) needs a decision from you today.

Where things stand:
- On 7 Aug the tenant, Elise Rowan, reported that the smoke alarm had come away from the ceiling (E001). The landlord, Ronan Vale, said he would send his own electrician (E004). On 12 Aug he said the work would be done "by the following weekend at the latest" (E007). That date has passed. We have nothing from him since, and the record shows no chase from us after 7 Aug.
- About 2 Sept the tenant told us a fitter came, took the bracket off and could not refit the alarm because there was no bracket in the box. No return visit was confirmed (E010). There is no evidence the alarm is mounted or tested (E014). On the records, the property has had no working ceiling-mounted smoke alarm in that spot for about 6 weeks.
- The tenant was in hospital from about 5 Sept and was discharged on 11 Sept. They asked us to stop contacting them while they recover, because the repeated calls and emails had upset them (E012, E013). We paused contact (E014). They may be a vulnerable occupant. This is not a clinical judgement. Their medical details must not go to the landlord or anyone else.
- On Sat 20 Sept the tenant rang us about someone who turned up unannounced, said they were there to "check something", and could not be verified. The tenant did not let them in (E015). We have not identified the visitor. The tenant says another agency contact passed it to building management (E016). We have not replied to the tenant in writing about it.

In this same turn I am: (1) chasing the landlord by email for the electrician's details, a firm date to remount and test the alarm, and whether he sent anyone on 20 Sept; (2) sending the tenant one short email that needs no reply. It says we are checking who the visitor was, that they should not let in anyone we have not named to them, and that we will only email.

Decisions that need you:
1. Safety and compliance: how long do we wait for the landlord before we treat this as urgent? Options are phoning him, or asking his approval for our contractor to fit and test an alarm now. Any spend needs his approval unless you hold authority to act.
2. The visitor: whether to take this up with building management or anyone else, and who from the agency logged the first report.
3. The tenant: how and when to contact them about access for the alarm visit while respecting the pause they asked for. That includes whether a person should make one careful call.

My recommendation: phone the landlord on Wed 24 Sept if he has not replied with a date by then. Ask him to have the alarm remounted and tested within 48 hours, or to approve our contractor doing it. One named person should then be the tenant's only contact for arranging access.
final.rationale: A missing or failed smoke alarm and a possibly vulnerable occupant are both escalation triggers. Here the alarm has been off the ceiling since 7 Aug, and a refit failed about 2 Sept (E010, E014). The tenant was recently discharged from hospital (E013). Three decisions need a person: whether to step in on the landlord's behalf (spend and compliance authority), whether the tenant's contact pause can be overridden to get access, and how to deal with an unverified visitor (E015, E016). The routine steps still go out now, as alsoSend. The landlord's promise lapsed in mid-August and he has never been chased, so a chase is overdue (E005, E007). The tenant contacted us about the visitor and is owed one low-pressure written reply with a date (E015).
final.expectedOutcome: Dorian takes ownership and decides on urgency, the landlord route and how to contact the tenant. The landlord replies with the electrician's details and a remount date, or is phoned on 24 Sept.
boundaries: Escalating does not fix the alarm or show that it is safe.
The visitor has not been identified and must not be assumed to be connected to the alarm work or to the landlord.
Nothing here approves spend on an agency contractor; that needs the landlord's approval or Dorian's authority.
The tenant's medical details are not shared with the landlord or any third party.
No finding is made about whether the landlord has breached any legal duty.
remainingWork: Landlord to confirm the electrician's identity, a remount-and-test date, and whether he sent anyone on 20 Sept
Arrange access with the tenant in a way that respects the contact pause
Get completion evidence (alarm mounted and tested) from the electrician or the landlord, and the tenant's confirmation
Tell the tenant who the visitor was once that is known
